get.description:
Return the chat's most recent workflow execution, or null.

The UI hydrates a chat's execution timeline from this route; a chat
with no launched workflow answers null rather than 404 so the absence
is not logged as an error.

schema.title: Response Get Chat Execution Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Chats  Chat Id  Execution Get

post.description:
Post a chat message and percolate steering when fields are present.

Steering is expressed only through chat messages: the persisted
message is the durable acknowledgement, and the service bumps the
intent epoch of the targeted (or all active) executions so the
orchestrator replans at the next safe model or tool boundary.  An
ordinary user message is the root conversation's ``send``: the
conversation persists it and wakes its own reply turn, so the reply
never runs inside the request.

get.description: Return the chat's durable sub-agent tree.
Return one node including its subtree.

post.description:
Cancel one node and its descendants, then stop its execution.

The cancelling operator is the authenticated principal the application
exposes to this router, never a body-supplied actor; a request whose
principal is not exposed fails closed exactly like the message route.
Already-terminal nodes and descendants are left untouched and are not
reported as cancelled, so the affordance is idempotent.

schema.title: Response Cancel Chat Sub Agent Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Chats  Chat Id  Sub Agents  Sub Agent Id  Cancel Post

get.description: Replay one node's activity, preserving the execution cursor.

post.description:
Persist one operator message for a chat-scoped sub-agent.

The answering actor is derived from the authenticated principal; a
request whose principal the application does not expose fails closed.

get.description: Return one node's direct children.

Return an ascending page, optionally scoped to one thread.

Without a cursor (or with ``after=0``), return the latest page. To
load all older history, repeat with ``before=nextBefore`` and the
same thread filter until ``nextBefore`` is null. A nonempty page's
cursor is its minimum sequence; exhaustion may require an empty page.
``after`` and ``before`` are exclusive and cannot be supplied together.

parameters.description: Exclusive forward cursor; cannot be used with before.
parameters.name: after

schema.title: After

parameters.description: Exclusive backward cursor; cannot be used with after.
parameters.name: before

schema.title: Before
